title: Polling & Real-Time Data
description: Set up polling for real-time data updates and learn smart strategies for efficient data synchronization.

data.text: Some applications need data that updates continuouslyâ€”stock prices, live notifications, or collaborative editing. React Query provides built-in polling capabilities that automatically refetch data at specified intervals, keeping your UI in sync with the server without manual effort.

data.title: When to Use Polling
items: Dashboards showing live metrics or KPIs

data.title: Polling vs WebSockets
data.text: Polling is simpler to implement but less efficient than WebSockets. Use polling when data changes infrequently or when real-time infrastructure is unavailable.

data.caption: Polling lifecycle with React Query
data.definition:
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Idle
    Idle --> Fetching: Component mounts
    Fetching --> Success: Data received
    Success --> Waiting: Wait interval
    Waiting --> Fetching: refetchInterval triggers
    Success --> Error: Network failure
    Error --> Waiting: Retry after delay
    Waiting --> [*]: Component unmounts

data.text: The simplest way to poll is to set `refetchInterval` on a query. This tells React Query to automatically refetch at the specified interval, regardless of whether the data has changed.

data.title: Polling with refetchInterval
data.content: The simplest way to poll is to set refetchInterval on a query

data.title: Background Polling
data.text: refetchIntervalInBackground controls whether polling continues when the user switches tabs. Set it to false to save bandwidth and battery.

Not all data needs the same polling frequency. You can use a dynamic `refetchInterval` function to adjust the interval based on query state. For example, poll faster when there are unread notifications, slower when everything is read.

data.title: Conditional Polling
data.content: Poll faster when there are unread notifications, slower otherwise

blocks.text: Users often switch tabs or navigate away. Polling in the background wastes resources. You can pause polling when the page is hidden and resume when it becomes visible again.

data.text: Users often switch tabs or navigate away. Polling in the background wastes resources. You can pause polling when the page is hidden and resume when it becomes visible again.

data.title: Pause Polling When Hidden
data.content: Use the Page Visibility API to pause polling when the user is not looking

data.title: Pause with External Control
data.content: Allow users or parent components to control polling state

data.text: When you need true real-time updates, WebSockets are more efficient than polling. You can combine WebSockets for push updates with React Query for caching and state management. The WebSocket handler writes directly to the cache using `setQueryData`.

data.title: WebSocket + React Query
data.content: Combine WebSockets for push updates with React Query for caching

items.question: What interval should I use for polling?
items.answer: Match the interval to your data's change frequency. Stock tickers need 1-5 seconds. News feeds can use 30-60 seconds. Server status checks can use 5-10 minutes.

items.question: Will polling drain the user's battery?
items.answer: Frequent polling on mobile can drain battery. Always use refetchIntervalInBackground: false and consider using the Network Information API to reduce intervals on slow connections.

items.question: Can I mix polling and WebSockets?
items.answer: Yes. Use WebSockets for high-priority real-time data and polling for lower-priority data where WebSocket infrastructure is not available.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Control polling with enabled and refetchIntervalInBackground
Always pause polling when not visible
Choose intervals based on data change frequency
data.takeaway: Real-time data requires balancing freshness with performance. React Query makes it easy to configure smart polling strategies.
